title: NLL-Guided Full-Attention Layer Selection for Training-Free Sliding-Window Adaptation

contributions.purpose: Decide which layers of a pretrained Transformer should retain full attention when adapting to hybrid sliding-window attention without training.
contributions.mechanism: NLL-guided layer selection: measure each layer's negative log-likelihood degradation on answer tokens when that layer uses sliding-window instead of full attention, and keep the most sensitive layers at full attention.
contributions.evaluation: On LongMemEval with Qwen3-4B, achieves 64.6% accuracy with only 1/4 full-attention layers, matching the 1/2-FA periodic baseline (65.0%) at half the budget.
contributions.source_quote: We introduce NLL-guided layer selection, a training-free method for identifying which layers should retain full attention in hybrid sliding-window models.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate that measured layer importance beats fixed periodic patterns and attention-based heuristics.
contributions.mechanism: Head-to-head comparison of NLL-guided 1/4-FA against periodic 1/4-FA patterns and attention-based heuristics (LightTransfer-style) on LongMemEval.
contributions.evaluation: NLL-guided 1/4-FA outperforms the best periodic 1/4-FA pattern by 10.4pp and attention-based heuristics by 26.4pp.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that NLL-Guided 1/4-FA achieves 64.6% accuracy on LongMemEval, matching the 1/2-FA periodic baseline (65.0%) while halving the full-attention budget, and outperforming the best periodic 1/4-FA pattern by 10.4 percentage points.

contributions.purpose: Validate that the NLL signal captures long-range attention needs rather than generic layer sensitivity.
contributions.mechanism: De-confounding analysis comparing layer rankings derived from long vs short prompts.
contributions.evaluation: Spearman rho = 0.306 between long- and short-prompt rankings, indicating the signal is specific to long-range attention needs.
contributions.source_quote: We provide mechanistic validation through de-confounding analysis, showing that the NLL signal is specific to long-range attention needs (Spearman rho = 0.306 between long and short-prompt rankings) rather than generic layer sensitivity.

contributions.purpose: Show the method is cheap enough for practical deployment.
contributions.mechanism: One-time NLL calibration pass whose cost amortizes over subsequent inference requests.
contributions.evaluation: Calibration takes ~15 minutes on 4 GPUs and amortizes after ~1,354 inference requests at 24k prompt length.
contributions.source_quote: We show the method is practical for deployment: calibration requires only ~15 minutes on 4 GPUs and amortizes after ~1,354 inference requests at 24k prompt length.

self_declared_provenance.quote: These approaches modify the attention computation uniformly across all layers, whereas our work selectively applies different attention patterns to different layers based on their measured importance.

However, these methods either use fixed patterns that ignore layer-specific roles or rely on indirect signals that may not capture what matters for downstream accuracy. Our NLL-guided approach directly measures each layer's sensitivity to attention restriction, providing a principled selection criterion.

notes: Positions itself as improving layer selection within the existing SWAA hybrid-attention framework (Yu et al., 2025). NLL-guided 1/4-FA slightly trails the 1/2-FA periodic baseline (64.6% vs 65.0%), framed as matching at half budget.
